the_tool_defect_that_ate_a_run.symptom: tri seeds ran two designs to completion -- one of them more than half an hour of place-and-route -- and printed a header with NOTHING under it
the_tool_defect_that_ate_a_run.mechanism: site="$(printf '%s' "$out" | grep -oE 'at BSCAN[0-9]' | tail -1 | tr -dc '0-9')". A failed build has no 'at BSCAN' line; grep exits 1, pipefail fails the pipeline, the substitution fails, and set -e ends the run BEFORE the row prints
the_tool_defect_that_ate_a_run.why_it_matters: the tool discarded the result in exactly the case the row exists to report, and reported nothing rather than ABSENT
third_instance_of_one_shape: grep -l exiting 1 aborted tri audit when the corpus became CLEAN (W979)
printf | grep -q inverted a successful SAT proof into a refutation (T834a, W982)
the_tool_defect_that_ate_a_run.repair: one helper that cannot fail -- pick() { printf '%s' "$1" | grep -oE "$2" 2>/dev/null | tail -1 || true; } -- and a row printed from whatever it returned, with an explicit ABSENT or CAP when the verdict is missing
the_tool_defect_that_ate_a_run.validated_on: the exact output that broke it: a FAIL/ABSENT stage line now prints a row instead of killing the script

the_second_defect_the_first_one_exposed.symptom: with the rows printing, two ABSENT results produced 'tri seeds: 0 pass, 0 fail over 2 placement(s)' followed by 'One verdict across every placement tried'
the_second_defect_the_first_one_exposed.why_it_is_wrong: ABSENT is not a verdict, it is the absence of one, and the closing sentence reads as reassurance. This project established the ABSENT/FAIL distinction in W977 -- 'the ABSENT/FAIL split matters: one genuine timing miss, not three' -- and the tool collapses it.
the_second_defect_the_first_one_exposed.status: found this wave, not yet repaired -- the script was executing while the run was in flight and editing a running bash script risks corrupting its parse
